Implementation summary:

**`src/setting/dto/cloudIAMAuthorizer.ts` (new)**
- `assumeScraperRole` – assumes the customer supplied `iamRoleArn` with the supplied `externalId` (via `fromTemporaryCredentials`).
- `validateScraperRole` – proves (1) the role can be assumed with the supplied external id and (2) the *returned* credentials can read the EC2 instance inventory collection uses (`getInstanceWithFilters` → `DescribeInstances`). Either failure throws `BadRequestException` with an array message mentioning IAM.
- `isCloudIAMDisconnect` / `cloudIAMNamesNoRole` – blank role = disconnect, a block that names no role is invalid.
- `resolveCloudIAMForSave` – returns `{ iamRoleArn: '', externalId: '' }` for a disconnect (external id cleared) and the validated block otherwise.
- `UsableCloudIAMRole()` class-validator decorator so bad roles are rejected by the global `ValidationPipe` (400 with a `message[0]` containing “IAM”) before the controller/service runs.

**`src/setting/settings.service.ts`** – `update()` now resolves/validates `cloudIAM` *before* reading/merging settings, writing influx points, running scheduler changes or setting the cache, so a failed check writes nothing else from that save.

**`src/setting/dto/update-settings.dto.ts`** – `cloudIAM` carries the new async validator + docs; **`settings.module.ts`** registers the rule as a provider.

**`src/setting/cloudIAM.settings.spec.ts` (new)** – tests against the local AWS emulator: good role saves, wrong/missing external id → 400 & nothing written, assumable-but-no-instance-read → 400 & nothing written, block with no role → 400, blank role disconnects and clears the external id, and updates that omit `cloudIAM` leave the stored role untouched.
